review.notes: Built on the course: COSO, three lines, fraud triangle, preventive vs detective, manual vs automated, SoD, authorisation matrix, P2P/O2C/cash controls, red flags, inherent vs residual risk, walkthrough, design vs operation, deviation rate, finding structure. Calculations checked. Fictional company.

content.company: Pinecrest Group (fictional), a distribution group with 4 branches and central finance
content.briefing: You join the internal audit team and lead your first audit: purchasing and payments at the largest branch. The audit committee wants to know if controls work and if anything looks like fraud.

variants.text: The branch manager says: 'With good controls, we can guarantee no errors.' What do you answer?

choices.t: Controls give reasonable, not absolute, assurance
choices.f: Human error, override and collusion can still beat controls.

choices.t: Agreed; that is the purpose of controls
choices.f: No control system guarantees zero errors.

choices.t: Only automated controls can guarantee it
choices.f: Automated controls are stronger, but still not absolute.

variants.text: Staff see the branch manager approving his own expense claims, and nobody objects. Which COSO component is weak?

choices.t: The control environment: tone at the top
choices.f: If leaders bypass rules, staff follow. Every other control weakens.

choices.t: Monitoring activities
choices.f: Monitoring may catch it later, but the root is tone at the top.

choices.t: Information and communication
choices.f: People know the rule. The problem is leadership behaviour.

variants.text: In the Three Lines Model, who owns and manages purchasing risk day to day?

choices.t: Management: first-line roles
choices.f: Correct. Internal audit gives independent assurance; it does not own the risk.

choices.t: Internal audit
choices.f: Audit must stay independent. It does not run controls.

choices.t: The board only
choices.f: The board oversees; management owns.

variants.text: The CFO asks you to design and run the new payment approval process. What do you say?

choices.t: Advise, but management must own it
choices.f: Running controls you later audit destroys your independence.

choices.t: Agree; you know controls best
choices.f: You would audit your own work.

choices.t: Agree, but only for six months
choices.f: Still a conflict for the period you run it.

variants.text: A buyer is in debt, the system lets him create suppliers and approve their invoices, and he says 'the company underpays me'. What do you see?

choices.t: All three sides of the fraud triangle
choices.f: Pressure, opportunity and rationalisation. Removing opportunity is your lever.

choices.t: Only a personal problem, not a risk
choices.f: Pressure plus opportunity is a classic fraud setting.

choices.t: Just a training gap in the system
choices.f: The issue is access, not knowledge.

variants.text: Which is a fraud red flag?

choices.t: A supplier shares an employee's bank account
choices.f: Classic red flag. You start an investigation with care.

choices.t: A supplier gives a 2% discount for early payment
choices.f: Normal commercial terms.

choices.t: A supplier sends invoices every month
choices.f: Regular invoicing is normal.

variants.text: Approval limit: Kz 5 million. You see 14 orders from one buyer between Kz 4.9 and 4.99 million.

choices.t: Likely split orders: test them all
choices.f: Orders just below limits are a red flag for splitting.

choices.t: Normal: each one is within his limit
choices.f: The pattern itself is suspicious.

choices.t: Raise his limit so the issue stops
choices.f: That rewards the behaviour.

variants.text: One clerk creates suppliers, records invoices and releases payments.

choices.t: Segregation of duties is missing
choices.f: Authorising, recording and paying must be split.

choices.t: Efficient, and the clerk is trusted
choices.f: Trust is not a control. One person controls everything.

choices.t: Fine if the CFO checks yearly
choices.f: A yearly check catches fraud far too late.

variants.text: The system blocks payment if PO, goods receipt and invoice do not match. What kind of control?

choices.t: Automated and preventive
choices.f: It stops errors before payment, every time, without fatigue.

choices.t: Manual and detective
choices.f: No person runs it, and it acts before the error.

choices.t: Automated and detective
choices.f: It prevents payment rather than finding errors after.

variants.text: A monthly bank reconciliation, reviewed by someone independent. What kind?

choices.t: Manual and detective
choices.f: It finds errors after they happen. Independence makes it stronger.

choices.t: Automated and preventive
choices.f: A person runs it, after the fact.

choices.t: Not a control, just accounting
choices.f: It is one of the key cash controls.

variants.text: How do you describe a control so it can be tested?

choices.t: Who, what, against what, when, and evidence
choices.f: A clear description lets anyone test it.

choices.t: 'Payments are checked carefully'
choices.f: Too vague to test.

choices.t: 'The CFO is responsible for payments'
choices.f: That names an owner, not a control.

variants.text: Stock adjustments are posted and approved by the same storekeeper.

choices.t: Approval must be independent
choices.f: An adjustment can hide theft. Someone independent approves it.

choices.t: Fine; he knows the stock best
choices.f: He can hide his own losses.

choices.t: Fine if the counts are monthly
choices.f: Counts help, but the same person approves the fix.

variants.text: Purchasing: inherent risk 20 (high). With good controls, residual risk 8. What drives the audit plan?

choices.t: Residual risk, then frequency by band
choices.f: Rank units by residual score and set frequency by risk band.

choices.t: Inherent risk only
choices.f: It ignores existing controls.

choices.t: Whichever unit is largest
choices.f: Size is one input, not the plan.

variants.text: Before testing payments, how do you understand the process?

choices.t: Walk one transaction from start to end
choices.f: Inspect documents and screens at each step.

choices.t: Read the policy manual only
choices.f: Practice often differs from policy.

choices.t: Ask the manager if it works
choices.f: Assertions are not evidence.

variants.text: The approval control is well designed on paper. What else must you test?

choices.t: Operating effectiveness over the period
choices.f: A good design that is not followed protects nothing.

choices.t: Nothing; design is enough
choices.f: Design and operation are tested separately.

choices.t: Only the latest month
choices.f: One month may not represent the period.

variants.text: You test 25 payments; 2 lack approval. What is the deviation rate?

choices.f: Correct: 2 / 25 x 100.
That is the count, not the rate.
You divided 25 by 2. The rate is 2 / 25 x 100.

variants.text: How do you write the finding on missing approvals?

choices.t: Condition, criteria, cause, effect, action
choices.f: Management can act on a complete finding.

choices.t: 'Approvals are poor and must improve'
choices.f: No facts, criteria or cause.

choices.t: List the clerk's name and mistakes
choices.f: Findings target processes, not blame.

variants.text: Management disagrees with your finding but cannot show evidence.

choices.t: Keep the evidenced finding; note their view
choices.f: Evidence decides. Their response appears in the report.

choices.t: Remove it to keep the relationship
choices.f: Independence is lost.

choices.t: Soften it until they agree
choices.f: Watered-down findings mislead the committee.

variants.text: Who may approve a Kz 50 million contract? The rules are unclear.

choices.t: An authorisation matrix by amount and risk
choices.f: Who can approve what, up to which amount, kept up to date.

choices.t: Whoever is the most senior present
choices.f: Unclear authority invites abuse.

choices.t: Any manager, to keep things moving
choices.f: Speed is not authority.

variants.text: Customer credit limits can be changed by any sales rep.

choices.t: Limit changes need independent approval
choices.f: Order-to-cash control: reps sell; credit decides.

choices.t: Fine; reps know their customers
choices.f: Reps have an incentive to raise limits.

choices.t: Fine if finance checks overdue debts
choices.f: Detective only; the risk is already taken.
